name: Frugll
old_description: Frugll customers are able to save over 50% on their solar installs.
about:
Frugll was founded in 2017 in Salt Lake City, Utah, by co-founders Jordan Folsom and Josh Giddings. The company operates as a direct-to-consumer solar installer, bypassing traditional sales commissions through a custom software platform that automates quoting and design.

The firm provides full-service solar installation and ongoing maintenance for residential customers, managing more than 190,000 systems across its installer network and serving over 1,500 homeowners directly. Its process emphasizes system design, permitting, installation, and post-installation support, all coordinated through proprietary tools that reduce overhead.

Frugll serves homeowners seeking residential solar power, with a focus on maximizing return on investment rather than monthly payment structures. The company’s customer base is built largely on referrals, and its marketing highlights average savings of 52 percent compared with other installers and typical payback periods of two to five years.

The company differentiates itself by eliminating sales commissions, using automation to pass cost savings directly to customers, and guaranteeing long-term system output. Its founders and a small executive team — including engineering lead Pascal Roget and operations head Bre Yamauchi — oversee a model that prioritizes education and transparent pricing.

name: Furniture Classics
old_description: Will be closing at 3:00 pm on Saturday, July 24th for seasonal maintenance.
about:
Furniture Classics operates a 10,000-square-foot showroom at 433 West 5th Avenue in downtown Anchorage, Alaska. The business traces its roots to the late 1950s when Anchorage pioneer Helen Calrquist founded Eckman's on 4th Avenue; after a bank takeover forced a relocation to 5th Avenue, the store passed to the Nerland family and later to longtime sales associate Erma Howell. In 1989, Howell partnered with current owner Colleen Hickey to establish Furniture Classics, continuing a lineage of female entrepreneurship in Alaska's furniture trade.

The company retails American-made furniture and home decor, offering same-day purchase from the showroom floor alongside custom-order programs that provide access to over 2,000 fabric and finish options. Complimentary interior design consultation is available for both showroom and custom clients. A three-person team — owner-designer Colleen Hickey, showroom manager Catharine Unger, and warehouse manager Garnett Morrow — handles receiving, preparation, assembly, and white-glove delivery across Anchorage, Girdwood, Eagle River, and the Matanuska Valley.

Furniture Classics serves residential customers throughout Southcentral Alaska, including homeowners seeking turnkey furnishings, clients commissioning custom upholstery, and design clients requesting full-room planning. The store sources inventory from national markets such as High Point, emphasizing brands built for durability in the Alaskan climate.

The company states its mission is to provide quality American-made furniture to Alaskans at an affordable price without sacrificing comfort or style, leveraging decades of buying experience to distinguish "heavy hitters" from lesser brands.

name: Furniture Industries
old_description: As a third generation family business since 1952, we have grown to become one of the nation’s most respected ff&e providers to the design industry.
about:
Furniture Industries, based in Minneapolis, Minnesota, traces its roots to 1952 when it began as a furniture manufacturing and reupholstery operation. The business transitioned to a third-generation family enterprise under Arnie Labofsky, who took leadership in the mid-1970s and instilled a culture of “do right by your clients and team members” that still guides the company.

Today FII operates as a full-service FF&E (furniture, fixtures, and equipment) partner for the hospitality sector. Its service lines span interior design, procurement, project management, logistics, and installation, allowing the firm to manage projects from concept through final fit-out.

The client roster centers on hotel developers and management groups. FII serves as an Approved Purchasing Agent for IHG Hotels & Resorts and a Procurement Services Provider for Hilton’s LivSmart Studios and Tru brands. Testimonials cite work with Douglas Carlson Development, Hotel Ventures Management, KM Hotels, Lighthouse Hospitality Group, Thomas Construction, Ehrhardt Properties, and Sonmar Management Corp.

The firm says its differentiation lies in “designing and procuring with purpose,” blending aesthetics, financial mindfulness, and schedule adherence. Clients repeatedly highlight reliability—meeting deadlines, budgets, and promises—as the reason they return for new builds, PIPs, and renovations.

name: Fusion EMS
old_description: Fusion specializes in turnkey and consigned EMS strategies, with a focus on high-mix, low-to-medium and high-volume production. We leverage deep expertise and a wide range of capabilities to develop custom solutions for our customers, and support your program every step of the way.
about:
Fusion EMS operates from Hillsboro, Oregon, in the Pacific Northwest. The company has spent three decades providing electronics manufacturing services, though a specific founding year and ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

Fusion EMS specializes in turnkey and consigned electronic manufacturing services (EMS), focusing on high-mix, low-to-medium and high-volume production. Its capabilities include conformal coating and potting, test development, box-build assembly, new product introduction (NPI) support, quick-turn prototyping, component purchasing and inventory management, and custom supplier strategies. The company emphasizes robust processes such as engineering meetings, alternate component sourcing, and statistical process control (SPC) with DMAIC principles. All production personnel are trained and certified to IPC Class III standards, and assemblies receive serial-number tracking.

Fusion EMS serves customers in aerospace, medical and life sciences, industrial, and military and defense sectors. Its services are geared toward original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) requiring high-reliability electronics manufacturing, from prototype through full production and product retirement.

Fusion EMS differentiates itself by offering custom solutions and supporting customer programs through every stage, leveraging deep expertise and a broad capability set.

about:
G&R Industries is based in Goffstown, New Hampshire. The company was formed in 1992 through the merger of two established industry players and has since grown to serve over 800 accounts across New England.

The firm provides beer line cleaning, draft system repair, glycol chiller maintenance, and custom draft system installation. Technicians perform routine two‑week cleanings, operate GPS‑tracked service vehicles, and carry stocked trucks for on‑site repairs. The company fields separate teams for cleaning/maintenance and for installation/repair, and supports clients with electronic invoicing and 24/7 emergency response.

Its customers include bars, restaurants, event venues, and other hospitality businesses throughout New England, ranging from single‑location independents to multi‑site corporate operators.

G&R emphasizes certified technicians, GPS‑tracked vehicles, thorough service checklists, flexible scheduling, and deep knowledge of local craft‑beer trends and regulations as its differentiators.

name: G. B. Woodworking
old_description: GB Woodworking, founded in 1982, is the continuation of a lifelong passion for working with wood.
about:
GB Woodworking, based in Boston, Massachusetts, was founded in 1982 by Gary Barcus as the continuation of a lifelong passion for working with wood. The owner-operated shop has served the Greater Boston area for over four decades.

The company designs, fabricates, and installs custom architectural millwork and cabinetry for residential projects. Its capabilities include built-in bedroom furniture, bookcases, home office systems, and closet doors. Work is completed in the company's shop using finishes such as precatalyzed lacquers, waterborne alkyd enamels, conversion varnishes, and catalyzed urethanes, then installed on-site with care to protect the client's home. Typical installations take one to two days, while larger rooms may require up to a week.

GB Woodworking serves homeowners and interior designers across communities including Boston, Brookline, Newton, Wellesley, Weston, and Pride's Crossing. The owner has collaborated with many of the area's top interior designers, translating design drawings into finished millwork.

Barcus emphasizes a client-first approach, offering no-cost design consultations, requiring no more than a 30% deposit, and providing shop drawings or samples for approval before fabrication begins. He personally oversees design, shop work, and installation, ensuring every piece receives his direct attention.
